newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says military can close off Hormuz Strait.
newsitem.headline: Iran says military can close off Hormuz Strait.

text.p: Iran has the power to close the Strait of Hormuz and control access to the key oil transport route, the commander of Iran's Revolutionary Guards said.

"We can keep the Strait of Hormuz open...But if we want to, we shall close this strait to anyone who is an obstacle to security in the region and keep it open for our friends and the Moslems," Major-General Mohsen Rezaei told Iranian television late on Saturday.

For more than a decade Iran's Islamic leaders have asserted the Iranian military's capability to close the Hormuz strait, the entrance to the Gulf through which more than 15 million barrels of oil -- half the world's oil exports -- pass each day.
Iran even made threats to close the strait at different stages of its 1980-88 war with Iraq, when at times Iran was also engaged in naval clashes with U.S. forces, but never carried them out.

Rezaei was speaking on television about the "Tariq ol-Qods" (Road to Jerusalem) military exercises, Iran's largest wargames which ended on Friday. His remarks were monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation.
"We proved that whenever anyone wants to create insecurity in the Persian Gulf, our combatants are able to neutralize this move very rapidly," Rezaei said.

The manoeuvres also proved Iran was capable of fighting a war on two fronts, Rezaei said. "For instance, we can both fight America in the south and, at the same time, if anyone wanted to take advantage of this American attack on our western borders, we are also able to be present there and foil that move as well," he said.
The U.S. navy keeps about 20 warships in the Gulf to enforce sanctions on Iraq and protect Gulf Arab oil states.
The three-day wargames were held in four provinces stretching from the Hormuz Strait to the border with Iraq and involved 200,000 guards and Basij militia volunteers.
